Persistent application caches

AppPaths owns the canonical <UserDataDir>/cache root and its children:

  • viewer3d/gdtf: mode-specific binary geometry.
  • viewer3d/meshes: binary model geometry.
  • gdtf/catalog.json: validated GDTF Share catalog snapshot.

Core's CacheService provides directory creation, statistics, cache deletion, legacy library cleanup and Viewer3D key generation without GUI dependencies. Preferences consumes this service; confirmation and translated presentation belong to CachePreferencesPage. Clearing is immediate and Apply/OK do not repeat it. Files under this root must be regenerable; settings, diagnostics, credentials, dictionaries, projects and libraries must remain outside it.

Viewer keys use full SHA-256 of length-delimited normalized physical path identity and GDTF mode, with separate model/GDTF namespaces. Binary headers retain format version, source size and nanosecond modification-time validation. Writes recreate directories after deletion. Existing runtime geometry stays usable; subsequent disk misses regenerate caches through the normal loaders. Catalog refresh reads disk each time and treats deletion as a miss.

The catalog migrates a usable legacy gdtf_catalog_cache.json from application user data (including the historical wxWidgets and temporary fallback locations). It validates before publication, preserves the old file on failure, and never replaces an existing new catalog. A migration marker under <UserDataDir>/cache_migrations/gdtf_catalog survives Clear Cache to prevent leftover legacy copies from resurrecting discarded data.

Startup cleanup runs before library bootstrap on the installed library and Perastage-owned user-data libraries, including the historical temporary fallback. Only files beside existing supported assets in fixtures, trusses, scene_objects and hoists qualify. Cleanup requires an exact asset-derived .cache or GDTF decimal mode-hash filename, a matching MSCH/GGCH magic and a known binary format version. Binary caches are deleted, never relocated. Externally configured libraries are excluded. Cleanup is repeatable; unrelated .cache files, orphan filenames and symlink targets are preserved.

Clearing recognizes Viewer3D SHA-256 .cache names and the catalog file and its temporary/backup siblings; unrecognized files are preserved and reported, even if placed inside the cache tree. Statistics and clearing report filesystem failures, reject symlink directory traversal and leave symlink entries untouched. Clearing recreates the required cache directories and reports partial deletion through the GUI. The cache root is exclusively application-owned: do not place user resources there.

Focused coverage lives in cache_service_test, gdtf_catalog_cache_test and preferences_dialog_test; the cache boundary policy test guards GUI separation.
